title: Congress sweeps Rajasthan's rural polls, beating ruling BJP in chief minister's home district
dek: Congress won about 3,750 panchayat samiti seats to the BJP's 2,200 and more than twice as many zila parishad seats, a year and a half before the state's next Assembly election.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Congress has won a clear victory over the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Rajasthan's panchayat samiti and zila parishad elections, taking roughly 3,750 of the 7,543 block-level seats and nearly 800 of the 1,275 district-level seats, according to results declared by the State Election Commission and tallied in reports over the weekend.

The result is the first statewide rural vote since the BJP won the 2023 Assembly election, and the party lost ground even in the home district of Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and in the districts of three Union ministers. The BJP said it accepted the verdict and would review what went wrong; the Congress called it the beginning of the end of the state government.

## What happened

Counting began on Friday, 20 November. By Friday evening the State Election Commission had declared results for 7,393 panchayat samiti seats, of which the Congress had won 3,701 and the BJP 2,181, and for 981 zila parishad seats, of which the Congress had won 599 and the BJP 301, according to reports citing the commission.

Later tallies, with nearly all seats declared by Saturday afternoon, put the Congress at about 3,747 to 3,758 panchayat samiti seats against the BJP's 2,211 to 2,213, and at 794 zila parishad seats against the BJP's 357. Reports differ slightly on the final figures because counting was still being completed; the State Election Commission has not yet published a consolidated statewide table.

The gap in votes was also wide. In the panchayat samiti polls the Congress received about 97.1 lakh votes (39.15 per cent) to the BJP's 83.8 lakh (33.78 per cent), and in the zila parishad polls 1.08 crore votes (43.40 per cent) to 93.6 lakh (37.77 per cent), according to one report's count of the results. More than 2.4 crore people voted, it said.

The Congress led in panchayat samiti seats in 33 of the 37 districts where votes were counted, and the BJP in four: Ajmer, Balotra, Salumber and Udaipur, according to reports. Counting in four more districts, Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar, has been put off to 17 December because the terms of their current councils run into next month.

Smaller parties took a significant share. The Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP), which has no MLAs in the current Assembly, won 497 panchayat samiti and 51 zila parishad seats, and the Bharat Adivasi Party 278 and 43, according to reports. Independents won more than 600 panchayat samiti seats.

## Setbacks on home ground

In Bharatpur, Mr Sharma's home district, independents won 76 panchayat samiti seats, the Congress 46 and the BJP 32, and the Congress won the zila parishad 21 seats to nine, according to reports. In the Sanganer panchayat samiti, in the chief minister's own Assembly constituency in Jaipur district, the BJP won three of 15 seats and the RLP eight, enough for it to choose the pradhan, or chairperson.

The Congress also won the most seats in both tiers in Bikaner, Jodhpur and Alwar, the home districts of the Union ministers Arjun Ram Meghwal, Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Bhupender Yadav. In Sikar, the wife and both sons of Jhabar Singh Kharra, the state's urban development minister, lost their contests, reports said.

## Background

Panchayat samitis are the block-level tier of rural local government and zila parishads the district-level tier. Their members choose the pradhans and zila pramukhs who run local development spending, and parties treat the polls as a test of rural opinion.

The BJP won the November 2023 Assembly election with 115 of 200 seats and 42.11 per cent of the vote, against the Congress's 70 seats and 39.96 per cent. In the municipal elections held in September this year, the gap between the two parties' vote shares was less than one percentage point, according to reports.

Rajasthan has voted out the ruling party at every Assembly election since 1998. The next is due by late 2028. The result comes as Mr Sharma's government approaches its third anniversary in December.

## What they are saying

The Rajasthan Congress president, Govind Singh Dotasra, wrote on X that "the countdown to the BJP government's end has now begun". Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, wrote that the result was "the voice of every village in the country". The former chief minister Ashok Gehlot said the results showed rural voters' anger over "government neglect and unfulfilled promises", according to reports.

The state BJP president, Madan Rathore, said in a statement that the party accepted the mandate and would "reflect positively on the election results and determine its future strategy". He said the BJP had focused on development, called the Congress's celebrations hypocritical in light of what he described as its "baseless allegations" against EVMs and institutions, and said Mr Dotasra and Mr Gandhi should apologise to the public. A BJP spokesperson, Ramlal Sharma, said the party's performance was "below expectations" and that it would look at its shortcomings, according to reports.

Chief Minister Sharma had not commented publicly on the results by Sunday afternoon.

## What happens next

The newly elected members will now choose pradhans for each panchayat samiti and zila pramukhs for each district; where no party has a majority, independents and smaller parties such as the RLP and the Bharat Adivasi Party will decide who takes charge. Results for Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar are due on 17 December.

## Key numbers

- 7,543: panchayat samiti seats; Congress about 3,750, BJP about 2,210 (near-final tallies)
- 1,275: zila parishad seats; Congress 794, BJP 357 (1,271 declared)
- 39.15% vs 33.78%: Congress and BJP vote shares in the panchayat samiti polls, by one count
- 4: districts whose results are due on 17 December
